item.text:
## 2B.8 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024

**Working judgment:** **Mostly real-security driven.** The 2024 record shows Marcos channeling defense spending and mobilization into **external defense modernization, coast-guard capacity, procurement reform, and self-reliant defense industry building**. I found **no credible evidence** of spending being used to enrich a patronage network or reward security elites. The main criticism is that the posture was also used for **deterrence signaling** and to project resolve toward China.

| ID | Direction | Title / Publisher / Date / URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Favorable | [PBBM to P5.768 trillion 2024 nat’l budget implementors: ‘Honor thy taxpayers who make the budget possible’](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-to-p5-768-trillion-2024-natl-budget-implementors-honor-thy-taxpayers-who-make-the-budget-possible/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2023-12-20 | Marcos framed the 2024 budget around lawful implementation, anti-overspending, and public accountability. This is evidence against using spending as a private-enrichment tool. | `2B.8`, `1B.7` |
| E2 | Favorable | [PBBM vows to capacitate AFP for external defense role](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-vows-to-capacitate-afp-for-external-defense-role/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-06-06 | Marcos said the AFP needed resources, training, and equipment as it shifted from internal operations to external defense. That is a plain real-security justification for mobilization. | `2B.8`, `2B.3`, `1B.7` |
| E3 | Favorable | [PBBM signs law for independent, dynamic, future-ready PH defense posture](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-law-for-independent-dynamic-future-ready-ph-defense-posture/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-10-08 | The SRDP Revitalization Act explicitly aimed to build domestic research, production, and industrial capacity for defense, with public-private and university participation. This is long-horizon security investment, not obvious patronage spending. | `2B.8`, `1B.7`, `1B.9` |
| E4 | Favorable | [PBBM signs laws on streamlining procurement, combatting online scams](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-07-20 | Marcos pushed procurement reform to shorten timelines, standardize forms, and institutionalize e-procurement. That cuts against claims that security and public spending were primarily a vehicle for graft or reward networks. | `2B.8`, `1B.7` |
| E5 | Favorable | [PH upgrading Coast Guard capabilities, modernizing the Armed Forces in the light of WPS issue, says PBBM](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/ph-upgrading-coast-guard-capabilities-modernizing-the-armed-forces-in-the-light-of-wps-issue-says-pbbm/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-03-04 | Marcos tied Coast Guard and AFP modernization to West Philippine Sea requirements and cited Re-Horizon 3 and the Comprehensive Archipelagic Defense Concept. This is a concrete security-needs rationale. | `2B.8`, `2B.3`, `2B.1` |
| E6 | Favorable / mixed | [PBBM arrives in Singapore to deliver key message for global defense stakeholders](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-arrives-in-singapore-to-deliver-key-message-for-global-defense-stakeholders/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-05-29 | Marcos described his Shangri-La message as one about the Philippines’ defense and diplomacy position in a tense region. That is consistent with deterrence signaling, but still framed as public security strategy rather than private power-building. | `2B.8`, `2B.3`, `1B.8` |
| E7 | Critical / mixed | [PBBM calls on ASEAN, other states to exercise boldness while remaining committed to international law in the South China Sea issue](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-calls-on-asean-other-states-to-exercise-boldness-while-remaining-committed-to-international-law-in-the-south-china-sea-issue/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-03-06 | Marcos urged boldness and refusal to yield an inch of sovereign territory. This is not evidence of corruption, but it does show military and diplomatic mobilization used to project resolve toward neighbors. | `2B.8`, `2B.3`, `2B.6` |
| E8 | Critical / mixed | [Philippines, US to hold military drills in islands facing South China Sea, Taiwan](https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-us-hold-military-drills-074919409.html) - Reuters, 2024-03-05 | Balikatan 2024 moved toward sensitive islands and added cyber/information-warfare training. That is deterrence-heavy and can intimidate neighbors, even if it is still defensively justified. | `2B.8`, `1B.3`, `1B.9` |
| E9 | Critical / mixed | [Philippines holds drills with allies after South China Sea confrontation](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/united-states-japan-philippine-conduct-maritime-exercises-in-south-china-sea-3758253) - Reuters, 2024-12-05 | After another confrontation, Manila held maritime drills with the U.S. and Japan inside its EEZ. This shows continued operational tempo and alliance signaling, which can be read as strength projection rather than pure need. | `2B.8`, `2B.1`, `1B.1` |

### Synthesis

- **Best evidence for 2B.8:** Marcos tied spending to **external defense, coast-guard modernization, domestic defense industry, and procurement reform**.
- **Best critical evidence:** The same posture was also used for **deterrence signaling** through exercises and alliance drills near sensitive areas.
- **What I did not find:** No reliable 2024 evidence that defense spending was used to **enrich networks**, **reward security elites**, or fund opaque patronage.

**Working judgment for 2B.8:** **Mostly real security needs.** There is a clear deterrent and signaling component, but the spending and mobilization record looks much more like **state defense modernization** than network enrichment or personal-strength theater.
